title: Stress: Definition, Sources, Types, Effects
summary: Stress defined, sources (cataclysmic, personal, background stressors), types (acute, chronic, episodic), effects (physiological, psychological), and Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome.
objectives: Describe cataclysmic, personal and background stressors.
Describe physiological and psychological effects of stress.
revision: Stress: definition, stressor sources/types, Selye's GAS (alarm-resistance-exhaustion), fight-or-flight response, stress effects.
traps: Stressors: cataclysmic (disasters), personal (life events), background (daily hassles).

notes.t: The physical and emotional response to demands (stressors) that tax or exceed a person's resources.

i: Personal: major life events (death, divorce, job loss)
Episodic acute stress: frequent acute episodes
Exhaustion: resources depleted, vulnerability to illness
Physiological: increased heart rate, blood pressure, cortisol, suppressed immunity
Psychological: anxiety, irritability, poor concentration, burnout
Behavioural: sleep disturbance, appetite changes, substance use

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about Selye's GAS stages, stressor types, and stress effects.

mnemonics.title: ARE
mnemonics.text: A — Alarm (fight-or-flight), R — Resistance (adaptation), E — Exhaustion (depletion)

flashcards.a: Physical and emotional response to demands exceeding resources.
